info.title: ideogram/p-image-ideogram
info.description: The request body Comfy Router accepts for the model "ideogram/p-image-ideogram", and the response body it returns. The INPUT schema is the same schema the server validates a call against before it reaches the provider, so what is published and what is enforced cannot differ. The OUTPUT schema describes the provider's native result document exactly as Router returns it: Router does not validate, narrow or re-envelope the response, so the output schema is descriptive rather than enforced, and Comfy owns no output shape of its own.

schema.description: Parameters for the P-Image-Ideogram text-to-image generation proxy request. The v1 `/proxy/` route reads these as multipart/form-data, which is also why Comfy Router cannot invoke this model yet: Router dispatches application/json only and refuses the call 403 not_enabled before validation. Use the v1 route until that changes.

aspect_ratio.description: Aspect ratio in format WxH. Supported values: 1x3, 3x1, 1x2, 2x1, 9x16, 16x9, 10x16, 16x10, 2x3, 3x2, 3x4, 4x3, 4x5, 5x4, 1x1. Defaults to 1x1.

enable_copyright_detection.description: Opt into post-generation copyright detection (Hive likeness and logo checks).

prompt.description: The prompt for image generation, either natural language or an Ideogram 4.0 JSON structured prompt.

prompt_upsampling.description: Prompt upsampling mode. Supported values are AUTO, ON, and OFF. Defaults to AUTO.

quality.description: Generation quality level. Supported values are VERY_LOW, LOW, MEDIUM, and HIGH. Defaults to MEDIUM.

resolution.description: Output resolution. Supported values are 1K and 2K. Defaults to 1K.

200.description: OK - the model's native JSON output, returned unchanged; the schema describes the provider's terminal result document as Router returns it.

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for the Ideogram models: Ideogram's generate response, forwarded unchanged. The generated images are in `data`, each with its URL at `data[].url`; `data[].is_image_safe` reports Ideogram's own moderation verdict for that image. Read the ELEMENT `url` rather than the `data` container — an element carrying a prompt echo and a seed and no URL is a non-empty array holding no image.
`routerresult/classification.go` classifies the `ideogram /ideogram-v3/generate` and `ideogram /ideogram-v4/generate` operations as direct-return, so `POST /v2/models/ideogram/ideogram-v3` and `POST /v2/models/ideogram/ideogram-v4` answer this document on the original call — there is no task handle and no poll. `/proxy/ideogram/ideogram-v3/generate` and `/proxy/ideogram/ideogram-v4/generate` return the same document, as they always have.
AUTHORED AHEAD OF ENABLEMENT for `ideogram/p-image-ideogram`. Router does NOT run that model today: its route accepts multipart/form-data only and `DispatchRouterTarget` dispatches application/json, so `routerresult/classification.go` deliberately has no row for `ideogram /text-to-image/p-image-ideogram` and `POST /v2/models/ideogram/p-image-ideogram` is refused with a `not_enabled` 403 before anything is validated or dispatched. The schema is published anyway because the document `/proxy/ideogram/text-to-image/p-image-ideogram` returns is already this one, so a caller reaching Ideogram through the v1 proxy can rely on it — and because a permissive `*/*` fallback would tell that caller nothing. The id is recorded in `routerOutputsPendingClassification`, which fails the build if a classification row lands and this paragraph is not removed with it.
Router does not re-host these images: `data[].url` is Ideogram's own link, forwarded unchanged, so it expires on Ideogram's own schedule rather than on a Comfy one.

data.prompt: A poster for a jazz festival, bold typography, warm colours

IdeogramGenerateResponse.description: Response from the Ideogram image generation API.

created.description: Timestamp when the generation was created.

is_image_safe.description: Indicates whether the image is considered safe.

prompt.description: The prompt used to generate this image.

resolution.description: The resolution of the generated image (e.g., '1024x1024').

seed.description: The seed value used for this generation.

style_type.description: The style type used for generation (e.g., 'REALISTIC', 'ANIME').
